content.text:
This looks like a gentamicin-type aminoglycoside (a gentamicin C1a/C1 analog), so I read it ring by ring.

**Left ring (purpose-built pyranose).** The ring atoms are C1 (attached to the glycosidic O), C2 (OH), C3 (NHCH3), C4 (CH3 and OH), C5 (CH2) and the ring O. In SMILES: C1(O-link) C(O) C(NC) C(C)(O) CO1.

**Central ring (2-deoxystreptamine).** Going around the ring:
- the top-left carbon bears the O link to the left ring,
- the top carbon bears OH,
- the top-right carbon bears the O link to the right ring,
- the bottom-right carbon bears NH2,
- the bottom carbon is CH2,
- the bottom-left carbon bears NH2.

SMILES: C1(O-left)C(O)C(O-right)C(N)CC1N.

**Right ring.** The ring atoms are C1 (anomeric, attached to O and the ring O), C2 (NH2), C3 (CH2), C4 (CH2), C5 (bearing the side chain) and the ring O. The side chain on C5 is CH(CH3)NHCH3.

SMILES: C1(O-link)OC(C(C)NC)CCC1N.

**Assembly.** The left ring's anomeric carbon is bonded to the central ring's O at the top-left carbon, and the right ring's anomeric carbon is bonded to the O at the top-right carbon.

CNC1C(O)C(OC2C(N)CC(N)C(OC3OC(C(C)NC)CCC3N)C2O)OCC1(C)O

Check on the central ring: C2 (O-left) – C(N) – C – C(N) – C(O-right) – C(O). Written as OC2C(N)CC(N)C(OR)C2O, the atom bonded to the left-ring O is followed by C(N), CH2, C(N), C(O-right) and C(OH), which closes back to the first atom. This matches the drawing.

No wedges or hashes are shown, so no stereochemistry is included.

SMILES: CNC1C(O)C(OC2C(N)CC(N)C(OC3OC(C(C)NC)CCC3N)C2O)OCC1(C)O
